ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Preventive Visit — Hatshepsut

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

text.paragraph: Ms. Hatshepsut is a 48-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes found eleven weeks ago, periodontitis, and knee osteoarthritis, who comes for the preventive visit booked at intake. The urinary symptoms settled within two days of nitrofurantoin, and she finished the five days; the culture grew Escherichia coli sensitive to it. She is ready to step up semaglutide to 0.5 mg today. Her extraction site has healed and scaling and root planing is booked with the dental team. Her periods have been irregular for a year, with occasional night sweats that do not trouble her. She has never had a mammogram or colorectal screening, and her last cervical screening was more than five years ago. [S]

tr.td: Metformin and semaglutide 0.25 mg; stepping up to 0.5 mg today

S — Synthetic presenting concern at the index visit, superseded by the dental diagnosis the next day. It echoes the dental disease reported on the mummy identified as hers (R, after the index date), without linking to it.
Acute periapical abscess of the lower left first molar (tooth 19), non-restorable, with a localized buccal vestibular swelling and no spread to fascial spaces; drained and extracted

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 20 minutes, with her consent. She wants full treatment for any illness from which she could return to her work and her household, and would not want her life prolonged if she could no longer know the people around her. She named a health care agent, recorded in the confidential part of the chart and not named here. To be revisited yearly. [S]
